headline: South Asia: War in the Gulf
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: War in the Gulf.
- Asia: Russian drones kill 2 in market outside Kyiv, 3 others in different regions, officials say.
- Western Russia: Russian attack destroys Kärcher warehouse in Ukraine.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 18 hours ago: Leaked sex tape costs software engineer a home.
The United States-based software engineer accused of causing the leak of videos and photographs of a sexual encounter with a Jamaican attorney has lost a multimillion-dollar home in St Ann, which has been sold to settle a judgment handed down by the Supreme Court. Rodrick Brown, who resides in New York City, could possibly lose a second apartment as the attorney, Kimberley Facey, has filed documents in court seeking to recover millions of dollars in legal costs she incurred in pursuing the lawsuit against him.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian attack destroys Kärcher warehouse in Ukraine.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russian attack destroys Kärcher warehouse in Ukraine.
Kärcher announced its Ukrainian warehouse was destroyed in a Russian strike on 27 September 2026, forcing the company to use alternative logistics.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian drones attack cars in Kharkiv Oblast: two killed, two injured.
A 67-year-old man was killed when a Russian FPV drone struck a car in Shestakove, Kharkiv Oblast, while his wife suffered acute stress.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Zelenskyy: Russians damage Saudi Arabian ambassador's residence.
President Zelenskyy stated Russian drone strikes on Kyiv damaged the residence of Saudi Arabia's ambassador, along with schools and kindergartens.
- The Moscow Times, 8 hours ago: Russia Hits Ukraine’s Largest Mobile Provider, Strikes Data Centers.
Kyivstar told Interfax Ukraine that its head office in Kyiv had been hit, but there were no casualties.
Southern Europe - bottom line: UK business minister warns potential US diesel export ban ‘significant concern’.
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: UK business minister warns potential US diesel export ban ‘significant concern’.
The U.K. receives around one-sixth of its diesel from the U.S. and would be one of the countries most exposed to an export ban.
- Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: EU rejoin push risks causing uncertainty, warns business secretary.
Jonathan Reynolds said the focus should be on improving Britain's trading relationship with Brussels.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Seven killed, dozens hurt in Saudi airstrike on Yemen market.
- Africanews, 9 hours ago: Seven killed, dozens hurt in Saudi airstrike on Yemen market.
Seven people were killed and 40 injured in a Saudi airstrike on a market in Yemen’s Taiz province, as Houthi forces advance and Saudi-led air raids intensify.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Sudan: RSF Drones Strike El Gezira Fuel Depot As Both Sides Report Shootdowns.
[Dabanga] Wad Madani -- Paramilitary Rapid Support Forces drones struck the Umm Alila fuel depot east of Wad Madani in El Gezira early on Sunday, triggering fires as Sudan's warring sides reported further drone activity across the country.
- Africanews, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: At least 27 people killed in two mass shootings in South Africa.
Gunmen killed at least 27 people in two mass shootings in South Africa’s two largest cities, police said Sunday, in the latest violence to strike the crime-weary country
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Nigerian foundation urges early screening in battle against childhood cancer.
The Okapi Cancer Foundation made the appeal during a childhood cancer awareness walk in Abuja, aimed at promoting awareness, mobilizing public participation, and raising resources for children battling cancer and their families
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Deadly strike hits market in Yemen’s Taiz.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Deadly strike hits market in Yemen’s Taiz.
A strike on a market in the Yemeni city of Taiz has killed at least seven people and wounded 40.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Israeli strikes continue in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire.
An Israeli Apache helicopter struck a commercial centre near Mayfadoun in Southern Lebanon.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Irish soccer team wears black armbands, refuse to shake Israeli players' hands during match.
The decision follows several conflicts amid the team, with players even demanding not to play the game due to the war in Gaza.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Herzog voices solidarity with Jerusalem Reform synagogue after repeated attacks.
Herzog told the community leaders that he would discuss the incidents with the Israel Police and stressed “the utmost importance of freedom of worship for all in the State of Israel.”
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: War in the Gulf.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: War in the Gulf.
THE war that the US and Israel imposed on Iran this year has failed to achieve any of the objectives that the two countries had intended. The declared purpose was to prevent Iran from building a nuclear weapon. A fact-check indicates that Iran had kept its civil nuclear programme under IAEA safeguards. It had also willingly agreed to a nuclear deal in 2015. It was President Donald Trump who pulled the US out of the deal in 2018 and re-engaged with Iran in his second term under a “maximum pressure” campaign.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Info ministry rejects Afghan Taliban's 'frivolous' claims linking Pakistan to reported Nuristan violence.
The information ministry on Sunday rejected Afghanistan’s claims of Pakistani forces’ alleged involvement in any “internal clashes” in the neighbouring country’s Nuristan province. “The allegations by the Afghan Taliban regime linking Pakistan with the alleged violence in Nuristan are frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth,” the information ministry’s “fact-check” account on X said.
- The Hindu - International, 17 hours ago: At least 7 dead as Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes and aerial war intensifies.
Russia has hammered Ukraine with missiles, glide bombs, and jet-powered drones, while frontline progress has slowed about 4.5 years after Moscow’s full-scale invasion
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Iran stands firm on Hormuz plan after US rejection.
Iran stood firm Sunday on its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, despite United States President Donald Trump’s rejection of the proposal that had created some optimism for breaking the Mideast war stalemate. The waterway is key to the world’s energy supply and is now central to the conflict between Washington and Tehran, which was triggered nearly seven months ago with deadly strikes on Iran.
Asia - bottom line: Russian drones kill 2 in market outside Kyiv, 3 others in different regions, officials say.
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Russian drones kill 2 in market outside Kyiv, 3 others in different regions, officials say.
Russian drones set ablaze a market outside the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Sunday, killing two people, while three others died in strikes by Moscow’s forces in different regions and Kyiv itself also came under attack, ‌local officials said. Ukrainian prosecutors said the drone attack hit a market in Sofiiska Borshchahivka on the western outskirts of Kyiv, killing two people and injuring about 10. Pictures posted online showed installations and vehicles on fire, with debris strewn on the ground. In...
- South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Trump expects new Iran talks despite rejecting deal offer.
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he expects talks with Iran to resume in the coming week, despite his rejection of a truce proposal put forward by Tehran. Iranian officials brought with them to the UN General Assembly in New York a plan for a seven-day truce followed by the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz shipping channel. Trump dismissed the plan and has mused on resuming full-scale air strikes on Iranian targets but he told the news platform Axios that he expects negotiations to...
- South China Morning Post - China, 11 hours ago: South African police probe mining feud shooting, 27 dead as elections near.
South African police on Sunday were hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country’s problem with gun violence. Officials were still establishing the motives for the shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town, but initial investigations suggested one could be a turf war between illegal miners and the other a business rivalry. Violent crime remains rife in South Africa, despite government efforts to curb one of...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 8 hours ago: Afghanistan says 28 dead fighters came from Pakistan as Islamabad denies ties.
Afghanistan’s defence ministry said on Sunday its forces had killed 28 fighters and wounded 32 in the eastern province of Nuristan after a group it said included Islamic State militants travelled from Pakistan. The ministry alleged Pakistani militias ‌had supported the fighters and that most of them were former Afghan government security personnel. Pakistan’s information ministry rejected the allegations, describing them as “frivolous, baseless and devoid of any truth” in a post on social...
India - bottom line: 2 Killed, 10 Missing After Avalanche Strikes Nepal's Himlung Himal Peak.
- NDTV - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: 2 Killed, 10 Missing After Avalanche Strikes Nepal's Himlung Himal Peak.
The avalanche at the base camp of the 7,126 metre Himlung Himal peak in the Nar Phu area buried a tent where nine climbers and 13 support staff were taking shelter.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: France steps in to protect Saudi oil infrastructure as Houthi attacks intensify.
France's military support to Saudi Arabia will involve deploying troops and defense systems to protect key energy infrastructure. The deployment follows repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities and aims to secure the Red Sea port of Yanbu. French official Jean-Noel Barrot emphasized that France's role is strictly defensive and does not equate to participation in the conflict.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Bank unions call off 3-day strike after assurances, IBA to study demands.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: BJP CMs counter-attack, demand opposition apology for its 'fabricated' campaign.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: (LEAD) (Asiad) Swimmers lament decision not to award medals to relay heat participants.
- Yonhap News Agency, 2 days ago: (LEAD) (Asiad) Swimmers lament decision not to award medals to relay heat participants.
TOKYO, Sept. 26 (Yonhap) -- By taking bronze in the men's 200-meter butterfly at...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Men accused of planning terrorist attack near RAF base used to strike Iran.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Men accused of planning terrorist attack near RAF base used to strike Iran.
Five men are suspected of preparing a terrorist act near an English air base the United States is using to strike Iranian targets.
- The Guardian - Australia, 2 hours ago: Morning Mail: following One Nation’s money trail; UK investigates suspected bomb plot; and legal help for NSW sexual assault survivors.
Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Politics, really newsletter. Good morning. In episode three of The Populist podcast, out today, senior correspondent Sarah Martin follows the money to find out why former insiders have accused the party of losing donations and lax financial oversight. Meanwhile, a new programme is being launched in New South Wales to help survivors of sexual assault navigate the complexities of the legal system as they seek to have their abusers brought to justice.
- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Get rules in place to hold data centres to account, experts tell Tasmania.
An artificial intelligence institute warns there may not be much economic benefit from data centre developments if public authorities don't put binding conditions on proponents.
- ABC News Australia, 4 hours ago: Banks cut rewards programs, free travel insurance amid surcharge ban.
Sweeping reforms from the Reserve Bank start this week, as banks hike fees and slash rewards programs in preparation.
